The CHFS Anthem transition FAQ (Feb. 5, 2025) adds that ProviderMCOInquiry@ky.gov 'is monitored and response is required same day.'

KRS 205.534(1)(d), as amended by 2026 Ky. Acts ch. 179, sec. 13, effective April 14, 2026, https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/Statutes/statute.aspx?id=57033 : MCO must allow 'any grievance or appeal related to the reduction or denial of the claim within one hundred twenty (120) days of confirmed receipt of a notification' (the 2019 text said sixty days); must ensure 'disposition of any grievance or any appeal within thirty (30) days from the date the grievance or appeal is filed'; 'Failure of the managed care organization to comply with subdivision a. of this subparagraph shall result in a fine or penalty as provided in subsection (6)'; and after a provider win 'payment is made in full to the provider within thirty (30) days from the date on which the appeal was resolved'. Subsection (6): fines, penalties and sanctions 'up to and including termination' under the MCO contract. Applies to every KY Medicaid MCO (statute is per MCO; Medicare and commercial excluded). Overrides the shorter manual windows (Humana 60 days, UHC Community Plan 60 days, WellCare clinical 60 days, Anthem 90 days).

KRS 205.534(1)(a)3-4 (same URL): for any adverse payment or coverage determination the MCO must provide 'copies of all documents, records, and other information relevant to a determination, including medical necessity criteria and any processes, strategies, or evidentiary standards relied upon, if requested by the provider ... at no cost to the provider', and 'a written reply in sufficient detail to inform the provider of all reasons for the determination.' Provider use: every KY Medicaid appeal letter can demand the full file and all reasons, in writing, free.

KRS 205.534(1)(c) (same URL): MCO must 'Reprocess claims that are incorrectly paid or denied in error, in compliance with KRS 304.17A-708. The reprocessing shall not require a provider to rebill or resubmit claims to obtain correct payment. A claim shall not be denied for timely filing if the initial claim was timely submitted;'. KRS 205.534(1)(e): audits allow at least 30 days for records, must finish within 180 days, and the MCO may 'Only recoup denied payments or issue a demand for payment from a provider upon the final disposition of the audit, including the appeals process established in KRS 205.646'.

KRS 205.534(3)(a)4 (same URL): each MCO must report monthly to DMS, 'For each internal appeal or grievance not resolved within sixty (60) calendar days, the name of the provider who filed the unresolved internal appeal or grievance, the dollar amount of the claim that was denied ..., the reason for the delay'. Provider use: an appeal left open past day 60 is reported to the regulator by name, which is real, citable pressure in a follow-up letter.

KRS 205.646(2), (3), (6) (effective July 1, 2025), https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/Statutes/statute.aspx?id=56581 : 'A provider may submit multiple claims to be appealed in a single external independent third-party review if the provider alleges that a Medicaid managed care organization has implemented a policy or practice that results in the denial, in whole or in part, of those claims.' The MCO's final internal letter must state that internal rights are exhausted, that the provider is entitled to EIR, and 'The time period and address'. Hearing appeal within 30 days; a multi-claim review goes to 'a single administrative hearing' and 'only one (1) fee shall be assessed' (fee cap $1,000). Note 907 KAR 17:035 Section 3(3) still says 'Only one (1) claim shall be reviewed per external independent third-party review unless the department determines ...'; the statute ('Notwithstanding any law to the contrary', amended 2019) controls. Provider use: pool same-reason KY Medicaid denials into one EIR.

907 KAR 17:040 Section 3, https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/907/017/040/ : 'Administrative Hearing Fee. The party that receives an adverse final order shall pay a fee of $600 to the department within thirty (30) calendar days of the issuance of the final order.' And 907 KAR 17:035 Section 5, https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/907/017/035/ : 'Within sixty (60) calendar days from the exhaustion of appeal rights after a final decision against an MCO, whether rendered in an administrative proceeding or a court of law, the MCO shall submit complete payment as required by the decision.' Resolves the researcher's $1,000 vs $600 question ($1,000 is the KRS 205.646(6) cap; $600 is the fee).

Anthem left Kentucky Medicaid: CHFS 'Kentucky Medicaid Anthem MCO Transition', https://chfs.ky.gov/agencies/dms/Pages/AnthemTransition.aspx : 'Anthem Kentucky Managed Care Plan, Inc. is no longer a Kentucky Medicaid Managed Care Organization effective Jan. 1, 2025'; FAQ (Feb. 5, 2025), https://www.chfs.ky.gov/agencies/dms/Documents/Anthem%20Medicaid%20MCO%20Transition%20FAQ_2.5.25%20DSNP.pdf : 'Anthem will be required to process claims up to 365 days post termination, as well as receive and respond to any appeals or grievances related to services prior to January 1, 2025.' Current KY Medicaid MCOs per CHFS: Aetna Better Health, Humana Healthy Horizons, Passport by Molina, UnitedHealthcare Community Plan, WellCare of Kentucky.

UnitedHealthcare Community Plan of Kentucky 2026 Care Provider Manual (Doc# PMI 05202026-094800; PDF 2026-05-20/06-15), Chapter 12 grid p. 69, https://www.uhcprovider.com/content/dam/provider/docs/public/admin-guides/comm-plan/KY-Care-Provider-Manual.pdf : a current KY Medicaid MCO the researcher did not cover (it received part of Anthem's members). Reconsideration: 'Claim reconsiderations (adjustment requests) are accepted within 24 months from the PRA', response '45 business days'; formal appeal: '60 calendar days from the provider remittance advice', 'Resolve within 30 calendar days. *May be extended by 14 calendar days.'; channel: 'We no longer use fax numbers.' (portal/API or mail); overpayment disputes to Attn: Overpayment Disputes, PO Box 740804, Atlanta, GA 30374-0804; 'In accordance with 907 KAR 1:671 ... providers have the right to an administrative hearing ... within 30 days of the UnitedHealthcare internal appeal determination' (907 KAR 1:671 itself not read). The 60-day appeal window is below the KRS 205.534(1)(d)1 floor of 120 days.

Anthem commercial (KY; same structure in IN) Notice of Overpayment and Claims Audit Appeal Policy, 2026 KY Commercial Provider Manual pp. 117-119, https://www.anthem.com/content/dam/digital/docs/provider/commercial/manuals/PM_KY_00011.pdf : refund within 30 calendar days if the provider agrees; 'An Appeal of the Notice of Overpayment must be in writing and received by Anthem or its designee within forty-five (45) calendar days of the date of the Notice of Overpayment unless applicable law expressly indicates otherwise ... If the Provider or Facility does not timely appeal, retraction will begin at the expiration of the forty-five (45) calendar days'; Anthem's response 'shall address each matter contained in the Provider’s or Facility’s Appeal.' Provider use: answer every Anthem overpayment notice by day 45 to stop the retraction (the researcher covered takeback rules for Humana, UHC and Aetna but not Anthem).

Anthem commercial clinical appeals, 2026 KY Commercial Provider Manual pp. 60-61 (same URL): 'Providers and Facilities have one hundred eighty (180) calendar days to file a clinical appeal from the date they receive notice of Anthem's initial decision.' and 'All standard post-service clinical appeals will be resolved within a reasonable period of time appropriate to the medical circumstances, but not later than sixty (60) calendar days from the receipt of the appeal request by Anthem.' This is the only firm Anthem commercial decision deadline found; medical-necessity denials (e.g., Mohs, radiation) use it, not the 2-year payment dispute.

UnitedHealthcare retroactive-eligibility refunds, 2026 UHC Administrative Guide p. 146: 'If we implement a claim reconsideration and request a refund, we notify you at least 30 business days prior to any adjustment, or as required by law or your Agreement.' Provider use: a retro-eligibility takeback without that notice is itself a dispute ground.

Does not apply: the 'Billing Dispute External Review Form' linked on Cigna's appeals page (https://www.cigna.com/static/www-cigna-com/docs/health-care-providers/form-billing-dispute-external-review.pdf) is a 2005 class-settlement form for 'Retained Claims' (services 'on or before May 27, 2005'); it gives no current external review for contract payment disputes.

Coverage gaps (no rule claimed): Indiana MDwise and UnitedHealthcare Community Plan of Indiana (Hoosier Care Connect, PathWays) manuals were not reviewed by the researcher or by me; Passport's 2026 manual remains unread (bot-blocked); the 405 IAC 1-1.6 text behind the Indiana 45-day deemed-approval rules was not verified here (Indiana area); UMWA Health & Retirement Funds and VA CCN provider dispute rules are outside the documents reviewed in this area.
